correctness.rationale: Exact multiplicative identity and the log-complete-subsum lemma reduce the large-prime tail to [1,P]. Five verified rational inequalities and Nagura’s 1952 prime interval theorem prove the needed inequality for every prime p≥11. The p∈{2,3,5,7} buckets split into exactly 32 explicit rationally specified closed intervals. The independent exact-fraction comparison script confirms every overlap, strict gap, and resulting 14 component endpoint codes using a proven Euler-product enclosure. The proof is for all positive integers, not a finite enumeration. The finite checker does not substitute for Nagura or the infinite subsum proof.

value.rationale: This gives the natural exact topological invariant of a concrete unrestricted arithmetic function at exponent -3, immediately after the previously studied first disconnected integer exponent -2. It identifies all fourteen connected components and their exact Euler-product endpoints, not just a finite sample or another sufficient condition. The finite small-prime stratification and interval-forming large-prime tail explain why the topology is finite and why this exponent matters.
